newsitem.title: GERMANY: KEY GERMAN SUGAR PRODUCER MAINTAINS YIELD FORECAST.
newsitem.headline: KEY GERMAN SUGAR PRODUCER MAINTAINS YIELD FORECAST.

text.p: Key northern German sugar producer Zuckerverbund Nord AG (ZVN) said it was maintaining forecasts of a beet yield of at least 50 tonnes per hectare in the 1997/98 crop.
"We have not revised our forecast, but it is based on the assumption there won't be an extreme summer drought," a ZVN official said on Tuesday.
Average beet yields in Lower Saxony, where ZVN operates, were 48.4 tph last year, when the average across Germany was 50.7.
Present temperatures around 30 degrees C were adding to beet weight but the crop was maturing overly quickly, a ZVN report said.
National sugar industry association WVZ in a statement on Aug 5 reported on the first beet test of the 1997/98 campaign.
It showed the national average beet yield to date at 31.2 tph versus 28.9 tph a year earlier in the first test.
The theoretical sugar yield was 3.93 tph versus 4.01 tph the year before.
The sugar content was down at 12.6 percent (13.9 previously).
The next test result is due on Aug 18 or 19.
